production.note: US model years: EPA data as listed by MPG Buddy (a database): "The EPA has rated the McLaren Automotive Speedtail for one model year, the 2020 McLaren Automotive Speedtail." McLaren (mclaren-speedtail-kennedy, 23 December 2019, reproduced by Automotive World): 106 Speedtails built at the McLaren Production Centre in Woking, "deliveries scheduled from February 2020".

body.note: Fixed-roof "three-seat cockpit" with the driver positioned centrally.

configuration.note: Quote: "The setup combines a 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V-8 and single electric motor, with drive sent to the rear wheels only."

displacementL.note: "4.0-liter"; no cc figure was found on an opened page. Goodwood (goodwood-speedtail): "4.0-litre twin-turbocharged V8 hybrid".

fuel.note: "petrol-electric hybrid" (McLaren reveal release). No opened page describes it as a plug-in hybrid.

drivetrain.note: "with drive sent to the rear wheels only"; Goodwood panel: "Seven-speed double-clutch, rear-wheel-drive".

transmission.note: Goodwood specification box: "Transmission | Seven-speed double-clutch, rear-wheel-drive" (McLaren SSG).

powerHp.note: Quote (McLaren release of 23 December 2019 reproduced by Automotive World, "SOURCE: McLaren"): "1,070PS (1,055bhp) and 1,150Nm (848lb ft)". 1,070 x 0.98632 = 1,055 hp. Motor Authority (Viknesh Vijayenthiran, 30 April 2020): "The peak output is 1,055 horsepower and 848 pound-feet of torque". Combined system output. At the October 2018 reveal McLaren quoted 1,050 PS / 1,035 bhp (mclaren-speedtail-reveal: "1,035bhp"); the final figure is used. powerStandard is DIN PS because McLaren's rating is metric, as in the Senna record.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (step 4). Quote (McLaren US release reproduced by The Gentleman Racer, "via McLaren"): "The low weight of the Speedtail – only 3,153lbs (1,430kg) dry – hastens this ability." 1,430 x 2.20462 = 3,153 lb. GTspirit (gtspirit-speedtail, Lawrence Adams): "1,430 kg dry weight"; Motor Authority 2020: "McLaren quoting a weight of 3,153 pounds". No McLaren curb weight and no major-magazine panel curb weight was found (McLaren's specification page did not load). Goodwood's review box prints "Kerb weight | 1,500kg", but its text says "a car weighing under 1,500kg", so it is a rounded upper bound from a single outlet, not a step-2 figure. No opened page says whether the dry figure assumes options. A car with fluids is heavier.
